Результаты показывают, что удары линеек: The results show that ruler collisions cannot be considered perfectly elastic. Theoretically, the ratio of displacements of the rulers should equal the ratio of the squares of their velocities immediately after the collision, i.e., determined by the formula {0} Thus, when a thirty-centimeter ruler strikes a twenty-centimeter one ({1}), the displacement ratio should be {#0}, while experimentally a smaller value {#1} is obtained. Even more significant discrepancies are observed for collisions of identical rulers — here theoretically the striking ruler should stop, but it continues moving in the same direction. Similarly, for the collision of a lighter ruler — it also continues moving in the original direction, although in a perfectly elastic collision it should move in the opposite direction. Thus, the ruler collision cannot be considered perfectly elastic. Apparently, the main reason for this (besides losses due to irreversible deformations) is the generation of elastic waves in the rulers during the collision. The simplest model of rulers that can at least qualitatively explain the obtained results is as follows. Replace each ruler with a pair of elastic balls connected by a spring. Let the elastic collision laws apply to the balls at the moment of collision. Then, even if the front ball of the striking pair gains velocity directed oppositely, the velocity of its center of mass may be directed in the original direction, so the striking pair as a whole will continue moving in the original direction.
